pr_target: dev (no PR — commit direct per AIPLA workflow)

features.description: Class Pydantic model with tag-namespace invariant validator. New file backend/db/models/class_.py + unit tests. Mandatory namespace shape: class:<owner_uid>:<class_id> enforced server-side at construction.
acceptance_criteria: Class.create_for_teacher(owner_uid, name) constructs tag_namespace=f'class:{owner_uid}:{class_id}' server-side
tag_namespace @field_validator rejects manually-supplied tags that don't match expected shape
Class.revoke() sets revoked=True + revoked_at; idempotent (calling twice doesn't change revoked_at)
camelCase aliases on all wire fields (classId, ownerUid, tagNamespace, groupCodes, createdAt, updatedAt, revokedAt)
Unit tests cover: happy-path construct, manual-tag rejection, soft-delete semantics, alias round-trip, two teachers produce different namespaces
features.notes: Class is reserved in Python — trailing underscore on module name. Field validator is the single security boundary. 113 LOC model + 177 LOC tests = 290 total (vs 130 estimate; overage is denser tests, not scope drift). 14/14 tests green; lint clean.

features.description: Firestore CRUD for classes. New backend/db/classes.py mirroring backend/db/chat_sessions.py pattern. Functions: create_class, get_class, list_classes_for_owner, update_class, add_lessons, remove_lessons, revoke_class, mint_group_codes_under_class, revoke_group_code.
acceptance_criteria: All CRUD functions covered by unit tests via the existing in-memory store fixture (no GCP credentials)
Soft-delete: revoke_class() flips the flag without dropping the doc; get_class() still returns it
list_classes_for_owner() filters by owner uid (teacher A cannot see teacher B's classes through this path)
mint_group_codes_under_class() writes both the anon_groups/<code> doc with class_id AND appends to Class.groupCodes; atomic via Firestore batch
features.notes: Pattern mirror chat_sessions.py worked cleanly. 254 LOC impl + 189 LOC tests = 443 (vs 200 estimate; same overage shape as M1 — denser tests). mint_group_codes_under_class uses existing create_group() and post-hoc updates anon_groups doc with classId. revoke_group_code drops anon_groups doc directly (next verify will fail). 16/16 M2 tests + 744 existing unit tests = 760 green; lint clean.

features.description: Teacher Firebase auth path. Extend get_current_user dispatch in backend/auth/__init__.py to accept Firebase teacher JWT alongside anon-group + LOCAL_MODE. Mark as auth_mode='firebase_teacher' so downstream handlers can distinguish.
acceptance_criteria: Firebase token with valid signature + email returns User(auth_mode='firebase_teacher', uid=<firebase uid>, email=<email>)
Existing anon-group tokens still dispatch correctly (regression test)
LOCAL_MODE shortcut still works (regression test)
Invalid Firebase token returns 401 with a clear error message (no auth_mode leakage in the error)
features.notes: Approach: instead of mutating auth_mode (would break ~10 existing tests asserting auth_mode='firebase'), added is_teacher boolean to User model. Firebase verifier sets is_teacher=True; LOCAL_MODE stub also marks teacher (consistent with 1.G-Ph2 de-facto behaviour); anon-group keeps default False. is_teacher is the gate for M4's /api/classes/* routes. No edits to auth/__init__.py dispatch needed — the existing logic already routes correctly. 8/8 M3 tests + 1419 existing unit/non-slow tests = 1427 green. Lint clean.

features.description: Eight new REST endpoints under /api/classes/*: CRUD + lessons (PATCH with add/remove) + groups (POST mint, DELETE revoke). Each endpoint enforces ownership; OTel span tag class_id + teacher_uid on every span.
acceptance_criteria: Each endpoint: happy-path test + auth-gate (no token = 401) + ownership-gate (teacher A cannot read/write teacher B's class = 403/404)
PATCH /lessons writes Skill.accessControl.tags for every added skill (appends class.tag_namespace idempotently — no duplicates on double-call)
PATCH /lessons with remove undoes both the binding (skill side) and the membership (class side)
POST /groups returns the freshly-minted group codes in the response body
OTel span tag class_id + teacher_uid set on every /api/classes/* span (verified via test exporter)
Router registered in backend/fast_api_app.py
features.notes: 8 endpoints live: POST/GET/GET-one/PATCH/DELETE classes, PATCH /lessons, POST /groups, DELETE /groups/{code}. Ownership gate returns 404 (not 403) on cross-teacher access to avoid leaking existence. PATCH /lessons writes both Class.lessons AND Skill.accessControl.tags — idempotent both directions. 329 LOC routes + 360 LOC tests = 689 (vs 350 estimate; same denser-tests pattern). 26/26 new tests + 1427 existing fast = 1453 green. Note: Pydantic shapes ended up in classes_routes.py rather than class_.py — kept the model file clean and shape-with-route co-locates request/response close to handlers.

features.description: Group→Class binding in backend/auth/group_id_auth.py. Replace hardcoded group_tags=frozenset() at line 175 with class-namespace lookup. Live revocation check: stale JWT minted before class soft-delete must be rejected on a fresh request.
acceptance_criteria: Anon-student joins via code bound to class with tagNamespace='class:T1:C1' = minted JWT carries group_tags=['class:T1:C1']
Anon-student joins via pre-v1 group code (no class_id field) = JWT carries group_tags=[] (today's behaviour preserved — regression)
Anon-student joins via code whose bound class is revoked=true = 403 with clear error
Stale JWT minted BEFORE class was soft-deleted is also rejected on a fresh request (live revocation check at verify_group_token layer)
Existing anon-group tests still pass (regression)
features.notes: The one-line edit at line 175 is misleading — the real work is the class lookup + revocation check. Test the revoked path explicitly; it's a common forget-to-check class of bug.

features.description: Backend E2E integration test exercising the full chain with the REAL AccessContext.can_access evaluator — no mocks. Slow/integration-marked so make test-fast skips it.
acceptance_criteria: Test creates two teachers + two classes; adds skill A to class T1 only; student joining via T1's code sees A but not T2-only skills
Student attempts to invoke a T2-only skill directly by skill_id = 403
Test passes against the in-memory Firestore fixture
Test marked @pytest.mark.slow + @pytest.mark.integration
Commit message records: 'AccessContext.can_access() unchanged in this sprint' (axiom 9 promise) — verifiable via git diff
features.notes: Proof that the design's primary success criterion holds: existing 5-type evaluator untouched, all new behaviour comes from the ownership/minting layer above it.

features.description: Frontend teacher dashboard. New /teacher route (index + per-class detail), useTeacherAuth route-guard hook, typed teacherApi helpers. Extend AuthContext to surface Firebase teacher token alongside (not instead of) anon-group state.
acceptance_criteria: Google OAuth sign-in at /teacher lands on dashboard within ~1.5s TTI on clean cache (manual on deployed dev)
Dashboard lists signed-in teacher's classes via GET /api/classes (real backend call, not LOCAL_MODE stub)
Create-class form (name + optional description) submits to POST /api/classes; new class appears in list
Per-class page: lessons multi-select queries /api/skills; Add/Remove hits PATCH /api/classes/{id}/lessons
Group-code minter: 'Mint N codes' button renders response codes in copyable list
Route guard: visiting /teacher without Firebase token redirects to sign-in surface (not the anon-group /group page)
Existing /group and /chat/* flows unaffected (regression)
Vitest green for new + modified tests
features.notes: 1.G-Ph2 teacher UI pages currently render against LOCAL_MODE stub data — this milestone replaces stub with real /api/classes/* calls. The 1.G-Ph3 LOCAL_MODE-removal swap is a SEPARATE follow-up sprint (don't lift LOCAL_MODE gates in this sprint).

features.description: manage-class skill — A2UI form authored as a chat-driven alternative to the React dashboard. Both surfaces consume the same /api/classes/* endpoints by design. Teacher-role tag on the skill keeps it off student skill lists.
acceptance_criteria: After re-seed, manage-class skill exists in Firestore with accessControl.type='tagged' and a teacher-role tag
Anon-student calling GET /api/skills does NOT see manage-class
Teacher (Firebase teacher JWT) calling GET /api/skills DOES see manage-class
The skill's A2UI surface renders a create-class form when teacher invokes via chat (manual check)
The agent's tool surface routes form submissions to the /api/classes/* CRUD
features.notes: Teacher-role tag is the access primitive — encode in the Firebase teacher JWT's group_tags at M3 (or via parallel path on User shape). JB/AR can pick React dashboard vs chat-form empirically; v1 ships both.

features.description: aiplatform class CLI family — 6 subcommands: new, list, get, lessons, groups, delete. respx-mocked transport tests. CLI authenticates via the existing aiplatform auth login flow (no new auth path).
acceptance_criteria: Every subcommand wraps the right httpx call with the right body shape (verified by respx-mocked tests)
CLI authenticates as teacher's Firebase token via aiplatform auth login (no new auth path)
--help strings clear enough to be self-documenting
make cli-selftest includes a class-roundtrip exercise (create → list → mint code → delete)
features.notes: Module name class_.py (trailing underscore) to match the Pydantic model file. Subcommand is `aiplatform class new/list/get/lessons/groups/delete` (top-level `class` is the family name).

waves.notes: Foundation; everything else depends on the Class model
Parallel: Firestore CRUD + teacher Firebase auth path, both depend only on M1
Single milestone gating the fan-out wave
Fan-out: group binding, frontend dashboard, manage-class skill, CLI — all depend only on M4
E2E test depends on M5 (real group→class binding)

parallelism.executor_recommendation_reason: Design-doc estimate is 3.7d which fits a single focused work-week. Parallel mode might shave ~0.5d but adds merge-conflict surface across AuthContext + skill seed + CLI that costs more than it saves at this scale.
